_doc: Curated classical-Chinese compound glosses, consulted by tools/build_word_gloss.py via longest-match prefix BEFORE falling back to CC-CEDICT. CC-CEDICT is modern-Mandarin: it systematically mis-glosses compounds whose classical sense has shifted (大学 = 'university' not 'The Great Learning'; 修身 picks up 'slim-fit'; 率性 = 'authentically' not 'following one's inborn nature'). This file supplies verified classical senses for the cases where CC-CEDICT is *wrong* or *absent* — not where it's merely modern. SEED SCOPE: title/opening compounds of each canonical book + high-frequency terms where the divergence is pedagogically damaging. Each entry must be defensible from James Legge's translations or a published zhuyin edition; when in doubt, leave it out and let the CC-CEDICT gloss (or honest null) render. Extend as more are verified. This is the word-level analog of pinyin-overrides.json (which fixes pinyin); this fixes gloss.
_format_NOTE: Keys are in SIMPLIFIED form, matching the chapter text (which is simplified — verified by inspecting content/books/*/chapters/chapter-001.json). This differs from pinyin-overrides.json which uses traditional keys; that file's trad-keyed stance is inherited from a now-stale assumption that the canon is traditional. If the canon is ever migrated to traditional, regenerate this file with traditional keys.
_references: James Legge, The Chinese Classics (1861-1872): Da Xue, Zhong Yong, Lunyu, Mengzi
James Legge, The Texts of Taoism (1891): Daodejing

大学之道.gloss: The way of the Great Learning

大学.gloss: The Great Learning (first of the Four Books); the learning of the great

明明德.gloss: to illustrate illustrious virtue; to make one's bright virtue shine

亲民.source: Legge, Da Xue (reading per Zhu Xi's gloss 亲=新)

止于至善.gloss: to rest in the highest excellence

平天下.gloss: to pacify the whole world (all under heaven)

格物.gloss: to investigate things (the extension of knowledge)

致知.gloss: to carry knowledge to the utmost

中庸.gloss: The Doctrine of the Mean; the Golden Mean (the constant middle way)

天命.gloss: the Mandate of Heaven; what Heaven has decreed

率性.gloss: to follow one's inborn nature (the way that is in accord with nature)

修道.gloss: to cultivate the Way (to cultivate one's moral path)

君子.gloss: the superior man; the exemplary person (junzi)

为政.gloss: to govern; the practice of government

仁者.gloss: the benevolent person; the man of perfect virtue

孟子.gloss: Mencius (the book or the philosopher, c. 372–289 BCE)

道德经.gloss: The Daodejing; The Classic of the Way and its Virtue (Laozi)
